issues: No integrity problems found. The diff does not touch the seed lines, the prepare.py import, the data, the evaluation call or the final summary printing.

The change is architectural. It keeps n_layer//2 unique blocks and runs them twice (block i % n_shared), adds a learnable 2-element loop_gate on each block's residual delta, and raises ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 80 (a wider model). Per-layer resid/x0 lambdas, value embeddings and window sizes are still indexed over all n_layer passes, which is consistent. loop_gate is added to resid_params, so the parameter-count assert still holds.

Latent bug that does not apply to this run: if n_layer is odd, i // n_shared can reach 2 and index past the end of loop_gate (size 2). If n_layer == 1, n_shared is 0 and i % 0 raises an error. The run finished, so n_layer was even and the result is valid.
Side note: gating the delta (x - x_in) also scales the block's internal residual contributions. That is intended and causes no harm.
The numbers support the reject. The candidate scored 1.1419 against the incumbent's 1.0989, which is 0.0430 bpb worse. The negative z fits a regression under a lower-is-better convention.

I can't recompute z independently. Each side has only one run and no noise standard deviation was given. The reported z = -5.549 implies a reference sigma of about 0.00775 (0.0430/5.549), which is plausible for run-to-run noise but can't be checked here.
The diff makes no claims that conflict with the numbers. The provisional decision to reject is correct.
